NASHUA SCHOOL DISTRICT 
POSITION DESCRIPTION   
 
Position Title: Head Teacher       Department:  High School  
Union Affiliation:  Teachers, Local 1044      Salary:  Stipend per CBA 
 
POSITION SUMMARY 
The High School Head Teacher will serve as an informed resource for content area and instructional best practices.  The 
Head Teacher fosters collaboration with colleagues and provides leadership necessary to implement curriculum with 
integrity and fidelity. 
 
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES 
Leadership and Guidance 
• Serve as a liaison between the department and administration. 
• Meet regularly with the building principal, department via regular department meetings, and district personnel, by 
attending district level curriculum meetings to provide updates and to assist in planning and implementing school 
goals and professional development. 
• Be knowledgeable of current pedagogy within content area and inform department members of practices, 
professional development opportunities, or methods of consideration. 
• Facilitate vertical and horizontal discussions within department and among middle and high schools. 
• Plan early release, in service day and summer work when applicable. 
• Maintain regular contact with counterpart at North/South High Schools to ensure consistency between schools. 
• Coordinate with school leadership and Director of School Counseling to update course offerings and revise the 
Program of Studies.  
• Act as an intermediary between counselors and department regarding matters of recovery, failure, and placement.  
• Oversee the department’s master scheduling process. 
• Facilitate the selection of students for department awards. 
• Lead the selection process of new teachers by screening applicants, attending job fairs, and conducting interviews. 
• Provide coaching and mentoring for teachers in the department. 
• Provide coaching, mentoring, monitoring and support long-term substitute teachers in the department.   
• Establish and maintain connections with stakeholders outside of the district. 
 
Administrative 
• Coordinate and oversee the purchasing and distribution of instructional materials and technological supplies for the 
department.  
• Maintain textbook inventory and technology resources for the content area(s). 
• Develop, review and implement curriculum and competency documents such as UBD’s, competencies, department 
wide rubrics. 
• Conduct review and analysis of data, e.g., demographics, SAT, SAS, enrollment, etc. to make informed decisions for 
the department, school, and district wide. 
 
Teaching 
• Delivery of specified course content using effective strategies for differentiation. 
• Interact positively, professionally, showing respect towards students and parents. 
• Actively engage students in lessons that are planned around grade level expectations and enhance critical thinking 
skills.  
• Implement instructional strategies that contribute to a climate where students are actively engaged in meaningful 
learning experiences.  
• Promote the expectation for student success, and inspire and empower students in their own learning.
Head Teacher Position Description 01/22 Page 2 of 2 
 
• Collaborate with peers regularly to align curriculum and enhance the instructional environment towards gains in 
student performance goals.  
• Engage in the continuous pursuit of new understanding of teaching and learning; reflect on individual practices and 
beliefs and engage in efficient work habits for planning lessons, meeting deadlines and honoring schedules. 
• Teach equivalent of three credits per school year, with a maximum of two (2) credits per quarter or semester, 
excluding Special Education Head Teachers. 
 
Other Related Duties 
• Perform other mutually agreed upon duties assigned by the Building Principal and/or District curriculum office. 
 
EDUCATION 
• BS/BA Degree. 
• Master’s Degree preferred. 
• Teacher Certification in relevant content area. 
 
QUALIFICATIONS 
• Minimum of three (3) years teaching experience. 
• Demonstrated ability to foster positive relationships within the school and community. 
• Demonstrated ability to communicate and work effectively with diverse individuals and/or groups. 
• Demonstrated understanding of best instructional practices. 
• Solid foundation of knowledge, skills, and disposition for the content area(s). 
• Commitment to participate in and provide ongoing professional development. 
• Ability to embrace, facilitate and implement district and school-based initiatives. 
• Ability to gather, organize, and analyze data for instructional decision making. 
 
SUPERVISION 
• Position reports to the Building Principal or designee and coordinates with the District Curriculum Office. 
 
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 
Physically performs sedentary work exerting up to twenty (20) pounds of force infrequently, up to ten (10) pounds 
occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects. Sedentary 
work involves sitting.  Position includes walking or standing for brief or intermittent periods of time. Occasionally reach 
above shoulders, kneel and bend. Mental demands requiring decision-making, analytical and organizational skills in order to 
achieve work objectives, draw daily operational conclusions, solve practical problems, use computer technology and to 
present information for use by students, peers and administration.   
 
NOTES 
• The Head Teacher will be selected from among the staff in the department in the school.   
• The Head Teacher will have one (1) teaching plan period, in addition to a minimum of (1) Head Teacher plan period 
per day. 
• The Head Teacher will not have any responsibility for evaluation of staff, bus or detention duties. 
• World Language (WL), Art, Health/PE Head Teachers will also serve as head teachers for middle school teachers in 
those areas. 
 
Revisions: 08/14/1998; 01/11/22
